Message shown to user: Both are anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs). Together they raise the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney harm.
These are both malaria medicines. Do not take two malaria treatments together unless a health worker directs it.
Both cause drowsiness. Together they can make you very sleepy and slow your breathing. Ask a pharmacist first.
Both contain sulfa medicines. People taking co-trimoxazole should not also be given SP unless a health worker decides.
Antacids stop ciprofloxacin being absorbed. Take them hours apart (see the leaflet).
Iron stops ciprofloxacin being absorbed. Take them hours apart (see the leaflet).
Zinc stops ciprofloxacin being absorbed. Take them hours apart (see the leaflet).
Antacids stop doxycycline being absorbed. Take them hours apart (see the leaflet).
Iron stops doxycycline being absorbed. Take them hours apart (see the leaflet).
Zinc stops doxycycline being absorbed. Take them hours apart (see the leaflet).
Antacids can reduce how well azithromycin works. Keep them a few hours apart.
Anti-inflammatory painkillers can raise blood pressure and make blood pressure medicine work less well. Ask a pharmacist.
These have opposite effects on the gut, so each can cancel out the other. Ask a pharmacist.
Fluconazole can increase the effect of amlodipine. Ask a pharmacist.
